- When sentiment is predominantly negative (≥15 consecutive -1.00), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 periods to reflect cooling.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., 1.00 after long -1.00 streak), model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–2% in first 2–3 periods to capture sentiment-driven rally.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed or weak; add 0.5–1.5% bias upward for first 5–7 periods.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops after peak), model fails to recognize it; apply 1–2% downward bias in next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 1.00s, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% in next 3–5 periods to avoid overbought bias.
- Model tends to lag in early periods when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias in first 2–3 periods to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
